item.text: {"search_note":"I found good evidence of institutional construction, but less evidence that these institutions were durable beyond Marcos personally. Most positives are executive orders, administrative reorganizations, or agency reforms, not deep constitutional or cross-administration settlements. I did not find strong direct evidence on whether these reforms were being insulated from reversal, independent of the presidency, or embedded in durable parliamentary/judicial/social bargaining.","evidence":[{"title":"Pag-Abot was institutionalized as a standing social-protection program","publisher":"Lawphil","date":"January 18, 2024","url":"https://lawphil.net/executive/execord/eo2024/eo_52_2024.html","summary":"EO 52 formally institutionalized the Pag-Abot Program, created an inter-agency committee, required a digital monitoring system, and mandated biannual reporting. This is one of the clearest signs that Marcos used bureaucracy and reporting architecture rather than ad hoc patronage.","question_ids":["6B.9","6B.8","6B.7","6B.5"]},{"title":"Pag-Abot was publicly framed as a lasting service-delivery system","publisher":"Presidential Communications Office","date":"January 19, 2024","url":"https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/page/177/","summary":"The Palace described Pag-Abot as taking street dwellers and other vulnerable people off the streets and helping them become productive members of society. That indicates a durable welfare institution rather than a one-time relief gesture.","question_ids":["6B.9","6B.8","6B.7"]},{"title":"PCIC was reorganized to better fit agricultural risk protection","publisher":"Lawphil","date":"May 13, 2024","url":"https://lawphil.net/executive/execord/eo2024/eo_60_2024.html","summary":"EO 60 moved the Philippine Crop Insurance Corporation under the Department of Agriculture and added farmer-sector representation on the board. That strengthens institutional fit and sectoral representation, which is a real durability signal.","question_ids":["6B.9","6B.8","6B.7","6B.5"]},{"title":"Procurement was pushed toward rule-based, auditable administration","publisher":"Presidential Communications Office","date":"July 20, 2024","url":"https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-signs-laws-on-streamlining-procurement-combatting-online-scams/","summary":"The New Government Procurement Act standardized forms, institutionalized e-procurement, and reduced room for favoritism. Because this is statute-based and system-level, it is stronger durability evidence than a typical executive program.","question_ids":["6B.9","6B.8","6B.7","6B.5"]},{"title":"Civil-service compensation was set on a multi-year schedule","publisher":"Presidential Communications Office","date":"August 2, 2024","url":"https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-issues-eo-increasing-salaries-benefits-of-govt-employees/","summary":"EO 64 created a four-tranche pay and allowance schedule for government workers plus a medical allowance. It is institution-building because it locks compensation into a scheduled framework, but it remains presidentially initiated and reversible.","question_ids":["6B.9","6B.8","6B.7"]},{"title":"Cyber governance was turned into a whole-of-nation roadmap with reporting","publisher":"Lawphil","date":"April 4, 2024","url":"https://lawphil.net/executive/execord/eo2024/eo_58_2024.html","summary":"EO 58 adopted the National Cybersecurity Plan 2023-2028, required agencies and LGUs to implement it, and required biannual reporting. This is a real institutional design move, though it is more state-capacity than social-institution durability.","question_ids":["6B.9","6B.5"]},{"title":"The NSC was reorganized as a “resilient” institution, but with heavy presidential control","publisher":"Lawphil","date":"December 30, 2024","url":"https://lawphil.net/executive/execord/eo2024/eo_81_2024.html","summary":"EO 81 explicitly said it sought a resilient national security institution, but it also let the president appoint additional officials and private citizens. That makes it mixed: institutionalized on paper, but still strongly personalized.","question_ids":["6B.9","6B.8","6B.7"]},{"title":"Rights-protecting institutions still looked weak under pressure","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"January 11, 2024","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/philippines-red-tagging-puts-activists-risk","summary":"HRW said red-tagging under Marcos put activists at serious risk and chilled democratic space. That undercuts a claim that the institutional environment was already durable and self-protecting.","question_ids":["6B.9","6B.8","6B.7"]},{"title":"Labor and civic intimidation persisted through 2024","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"September 25, 2024","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/09/25/philippines-dangerous-red-tagging-labor-leaders","summary":"HRW reported officials and security actors threatened union leaders and other vulnerable groups. That is strong evidence that formal institutions were not yet reliably protecting dignity or pluralism.","question_ids":["6B.9","6B.8","6B.7"]},{"title":"Independent monitors still judged the broader environment incomplete","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2024","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/philippines/freedom-world/2024","summary":"Freedom House said red-tagging persisted, protections for Indigenous people, LGBT+ people, and disability rights were weak, and representation remained concentrated in political families. That is negative evidence for durable, impersonal institutions.","question_ids":["6B.9","6B.8","6B.7"]},{"title":"Abuse and fear remained embedded despite reform rhetoric","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"October 14, 2024","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/asa35/8574/2024/en/","summary":"Amnesty said Marcos-era actors weaponized misinformation and anti-terror framing to create fear. That is evidence against a clean transition to durable, rights-bearing institutions.","question_ids":["6B.9","6B.8","6B.7"]},{"title":"Executive-led accountability was real, but incomplete","publisher":"Philippine News Agency","date":"November 6, 2024","url":"https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1237266","summary":"The DOJ created a task force to investigate extrajudicial killings and file charges if warranted. This is a genuine institutional move, but it remained executive-led rather than independently entrenched.","question_ids":["6B.9","6B.8","6B.7"]}]}
